query:
One group member argued that using running technology during a run is counterproductive to performance. Who made this specific claim, and what distinguishes their reasoning from a similar view expressed in the same exchange?

Options:
A. Rafe
B. Leo
C. Tom
D. Cass
context:
[1] (about=Rafe, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:14:00) Right so I've been thinking about GPS watches and long run training, and I'm not convinced they're worth the data overload. You end up running to satisfy the watch rather than actually running.
[2] (about=Tom, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:15:00) Same. Strava segment after is enough. Gadgets slow you down mentally.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:16:00) Oh not this debate again 😂 Leo backs the data, Tom and Rafe back their feelings haha
[4] (about=Leo, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:17:00) Heart rate zones are not optional for marathon training at our age. The data removes guesswork.
[5] (about=Tom, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:19:00) Team no-overthinking.
[6] (about=Rafe, episodic, t6 @2025-09-28T11:20:00) Team aesthetics. Which frankly is the superior approach to most things.
[7] (about=Yuki, episodic, t10 @2025-10-12T10:22:00) That is consistent with the research on pacing strategy. Negative splits outperform even-effort by approximately 2-4% in recreational runners.
[8] (about=Rafe, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:50:00) Here's the thing, I was at the finish line, I did not run a race, and I am still absolutely in for both. This feels like the correct reward structure.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:34:00) Rafe I saw the sign from about 200m out and it made me run faster I think 😂 also it said 'GO RIDGELINE RUNNERS' in massive letters which is exactly the correct energy
[10] (about=Rafe, episodic, t12 @2025-10-19T09:33:00) Right so I am not running it in the end, scheduling issues, but I will be at the finish line with adequate hydration and a sign. You have my full moral support.
[11] (about=Rafe, core, t6 @2025-09-28T11:01:00) Not convinced GPS watches are worth the data overload; running to satisfy the watch rather than actually running.
[12] (about=Tom, core, t10 @2025-10-12T10:16:00) Ran 2 minutes faster over 16km than the same route in September, with less perceived effort in the last 3km.
